# CI Adoption Notes

This page captures the operational rules learned while moving existing
Codeberg-hosted Rust repositories from hand-rolled Forgejo Actions workflows to
`simit init ci`.

## Generator Contract

Generated workflow files are owned by simit and include:

```text
# Generated by simit. Manual edits will be reported as ci=drift.
```

After the first non-check `simit init ci` run, simit persists the effective CI
options into `simit.toml` under `[ci]`. The canonical drift check is then:

```sh
simit init ci --platform <forgejo|github> --check --diff
```

When a project has not yet persisted its CI options, the drift error still
prints the full regeneration command with the effective runtime, runner,
workspace, and optional gates so the migration path stays explicit.

Persisted CI settings look like:

```toml
[ci]
platform = "forgejo"
runtime = "nix"
runner = "atlas"
workspace = true
with_deny = true
with_audit = true
with_docs = true
with_msrv = true
```

## Generic CI vs Release Publishing

Rust CI and crates.io publishing are separate modes. By default, `simit init ci`
generates ordinary CI workflows even when a package has crates.io metadata. It
does not generate `publish-crate*.yaml` or `keys/maintainers.gpg` unless release
publishing is enabled explicitly or inferred from existing generated release
workflows.

Enable crates.io release workflows with:

```sh
simit init ci --platform forgejo --publish-crates
```

Persist the choice when a project owns release publishing:

```toml
[ci]
publish_crates = true
```

Pass `--publish-crates=false` or set `publish_crates = false` to keep a project
CI-only even when stale generated publish workflows are present. Release
artifact and package-manager publishing flags such as `--with-artifacts`,
`--with-homebrew`, `--with-chocolatey`, and `--with-scoop` imply release mode.

For a Forgejo Nix workspace with release artifacts and cargo-deny:

```sh
simit init ci --platform forgejo --runtime nix --runner atlas-nix-trusted \
  --workspace --with-artifacts --with-deny --check --diff
```

If the project also publishes a Homebrew tap, keep the tap metadata in project
config when possible. Command-line overrides work, but config makes future
checks shorter and reproducible.

## Flake-Integrated Rust Projects

`--runtime auto` selects the Nix runtime when `flake.nix` exposes meaningful
project outputs such as `packages`, `apps`, `checks`, `devShells`, NixOS or
Home Manager modules, or top-level `lib`. Cargo-only projects and placeholder
flakes stay on direct Cargo CI.

For existing custom flakes, keep project-owned outputs intact and let simit
manage hook wiring with:

```sh
simit init flake --scope hooks-only
simit init ci --platform forgejo --runtime nix
```

## Non-Publishable Crates

Cargo represents `publish = false` in metadata as an empty `publish` list.
Simit treats that as a hard opt-out from crates.io publication:

- CI still runs tests, optional policy gates, and clippy for the package.
- CI skips `cargo package` for that package.
- Simit does not generate `publish-crate-<package>.yaml` for that package.

This matters for workspace utility crates such as `xtask`. They often depend on
unpublished git-only helper crates, so `cargo package -p xtask` fails even
though the crate is intentionally not publishable.

When converting a workspace, delete any stale generated `publish-crate-*.yaml`
for `publish = false` members after regenerating CI. Check mode reports those
stale generated files as `extra`.

## Cargo-Deny Policy

`--with-deny` means generated workflows install and run:

```sh
cargo deny check bans licenses sources
```

The policy file is project-owned:

- If `deny.toml` is missing, simit bootstraps a conservative default.
- If `deny.toml` already exists, simit leaves it alone.
- Check mode does not treat local license or source allow-list changes as
  generated CI drift.

Validate policy changes with the same cargo-deny version used by generated CI:

```sh
CARGO_HOME=/tmp/simit-cargo-deny-0183
cargo install cargo-deny --locked --version 0.18.3
"$CARGO_HOME/bin/cargo-deny" check bans licenses sources
```

Do not assume a newer local `cargo-deny` accepts the same license identifiers as
the pinned CI version. For example, `cargo-deny 0.18.3` expects the older GPL
allow-list spelling `GPL-3.0` rather than `GPL-3.0-only`.

## Forgejo Nix Runtime Details

Forgejo Nix-runtime workflows intentionally set:

```yaml
env:
  NIX_CONFIG: "experimental-features = nix-command flakes"
  XDG_CACHE_HOME: "/tmp/.cache"
  CARGO_HOME: "/tmp/.cargo"
```

`CARGO_HOME` must be absolute. Relative cargo homes can make `cargo install`
panic or write into surprising paths under Forgejo/act containers.

Generated Nix-runtime workflows also add `$CARGO_HOME/bin` to `PATH` before
installing optional cargo tools. Optional tools should be installed into the
workflow cargo home, not assumed from the runner image.

MSRV checks under Nix use the dev shell's cargo:

```sh
nix develop -c cargo check --all-targets
```

They do not use `cargo +<msrv>` because Nix dev shells do not imply rustup
toolchains.

### Nix-runtime Cargo cache

Projects whose Nix-runtime workflow runs a substantial host-side Cargo gate can
provide a project-owned Cargo command while retaining the Nix flake gate:

```toml
[ci]
check_command = "cargo xtask ci"
```

`check_command` replaces only Simit's generic Cargo lane. Nix-runtime workflows
still run `nix flake check` by default. Projects with a deliberately focused
Nix validation workflow may opt out explicitly:

```toml
[ci]
check_command = "cargo run --locked -p syndb-ci -- ci"
nix_flake_check = false
```

Projects whose Nix-runtime workflow runs a substantial host-side Cargo gate can
also opt into a registry and target cache:

```toml
[ci]
runtime = "nix"
with_nix_cargo_cache = true
```

The generated workflow caches `/tmp/.cargo/registry`, `/tmp/.cargo/git`, and
the workspace `target/` directory. The key includes the lockfiles, flake,
Rust toolchain, Cargo configuration, runner architecture, and generated job
scope. The option is deliberately opt-in because projects that install mutable
Cargo tools into the generated Cargo home may prefer the existing tool-cache
behavior. It cannot be combined with custom `CARGO_HOME` or
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR` workflow environment overrides.

## Cargo-Audit Reliability

Generated cargo-audit steps fetch the RustSec advisory database explicitly and
then run audit with a local database:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/RustSec/advisory-db.git "$db"
cargo audit --db "$db" --no-fetch --stale
```

This avoids repeated network fetch behavior inside `cargo audit` itself and
makes failures easier to separate into "could not fetch advisory DB" versus
"advisory gate failed".

## Runner Debugging

When Codeberg/Forgejo runners are flaky, separate stale runs from fresh runs:

1. Push or rerun on a new commit so the head SHA changes.
2. Poll only runs created for that head.
3. Inspect exact run logs before changing code.

Use the repository metadata command first when using the Codeberg workflow:

```sh
berg --owner-repo caniko/<repo> repo info
```

Then poll runs through the Codeberg API if the local `berg` build does not have
Actions subcommands:

```sh
curl -fsSL "https://codeberg.org/api/v1/repos/caniko/<repo>/actions/runs?limit=10" |
  jq -r '.workflow_runs[] | [.id, (.html_url|split("/")[-1]), .status, .workflow_id] | @tsv'
```

A failure like `Input/output error (os error 5)` while rustc writes metadata is
runner/storage instability. A failure from `cargo package`, `cargo deny`, or a
crate test is a project or generator issue until reproduced otherwise.

## Fleet Adoption Checklist

For each repository:

1. Rebase the adoption branch onto the default branch.
2. Regenerate CI with the project's intended options.
3. Run `simit init ci ... --check --diff`.
4. Run the relevant local package checks that failed in CI.
5. Push one repo-scoped branch.
6. Watch fresh Codeberg runs for that branch head only.
7. After merge, verify at least one green default-branch CI run.

Fleet-level verification:

```sh
simit projects scan
simit projects list
```

The converted repositories should no longer show `ci(hand-rolled)`. Projects
with only generated workflows show `ci(managed)`. Projects with generated CI
plus supplementary non-generated workflows show `ci(managed+extra)`.
